{{short description|Tetrahedron where all three face angles at one vertex are right angles}}
[[File:2D-simplex.svg|thumb|A trirectangular tetrahedron with its base shown in green and its apex as a solid black disk. It can be constructed by a coordinate [[octant (solid geometry)|octant]] and a plane crossing all 3 axes away from the origin (''x''>0; ''y''>0; ''z''>0) and ''x/a+y/b+z/c''<1]]

In [[geometry]], a '''trirectangular tetrahedron''' is a [[tetrahedron]] where all three [[Face (geometry)|face]] [[plane angle|angles]] at one [[Vertex (geometry)|vertex]] are [[right angles]]. That vertex is called the ''right angle'' or [[apex (geometry)|''apex'']] of the trirectangular tetrahedron and the face opposite it is called the ''[[base (geometry)|base]]''. The three [[Edge (geometry)|edges]] that meet at the right angle are called the ''legs'' and the perpendicular from the right angle to the base is called the ''altitude'' of the tetrahedron (analogous to the [[altitude (triangle)|altitude]] of a triangle).

[[File:Kepler's tetrahedron in cube.png|thumb|280px|Kepler's drawing of a [[regular tetrahedron]] inscribed in a cube (on the left), and one of the four trirectangular tetrahedra that surround it (on the right), filling the cube.]]
An example of a trirectangular tetrahedron is a [[Truncation (geometry)|truncated]] [[solid figure]] near the corner of a [[cube]] or an [[octant (geometry)|octant]] at the origin of [[Euclidean space]].
[[Johannes Kepler|Kepler]] discovered the relationship between the cube, regular tetrahedron and trirectangular tetrahedron.<ref>{{cite book|title=Harmonices Mundi|first=Johannes|last=Kepler|author-link=Johannes Kepler|title-link=Harmonices Mundi|year=1619|language=la|page=[https://archive.org/details/ioanniskepplerih00kepl/page/180 181]}}</ref>

Only the bifurcating graph of the <math>B_3</math> [[Coxeter group#Affine Coxeter groups|affine Coxeter group]] has a Trirectangular tetrahedron fundamental domain.

==Metric formulas==
If the legs have lengths x'', y, z'' then the trirectangular tetrahedron has the [[volume]]<ref>{{cite book |title=An Excursion through Elementary Mathematics, Volume II: Euclidean Geometry |author1=Antonio Caminha Muniz Neto |edition= |publisher=Springer |year=2018 |isbn=978-3-319-77974-4 |page=437 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AtpVDwAAQBAJ}} [https://books.google.com/books?id=AtpVDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA437 Problem 3 on page 437]</ref>

:<math>V=\frac{xyz}{6}.</math>

The altitude ''h'' satisfies<ref>Eves, Howard Whitley, "Great moments in mathematics (before 1650)", ''Mathematical Association of America'', 1983, p. 41.</ref>

:<math>\frac{1}{h^2}=\frac{1}{x^2}+\frac{1}{y^2}+\frac{1}{z^2}.</math>

The area <math>T_0</math> of the base is given by<ref>[https://gogeometry.com/pythagoras/right_triangle_formulas_facts.htm Gutierrez, Antonio, "Right Triangle Formulas"]</ref>

:<math>T_0=\frac{xyz}{2h}.</math>

The [[solid angle]] at the right-angled vertex, from which the opposite face (the base) subtends an [[octant of a sphere|octant]], has measure {{pi}}/2&nbsp; [[steradian]]s, one eighth of the surface area of a [[unit sphere]].

==De Gua's theorem==
{{main|De Gua's theorem}}
If the [[area]] of the base is <math>T_0</math> and the areas of the three other (right-angled) faces are <math>T_1</math>, <math>T_2</math> and <math>T_3</math>, then

:<math>T_0^2=T_1^2+T_2^2+T_3^2.</math>

This is a generalization of the [[Pythagorean theorem]] to a tetrahedron.

==Integer solution==
===Integer edges===
Trirectangular tetrahedra with integer legs <math>a,b,c</math> and sides <math>d=\sqrt{b^2+c^2}, e=\sqrt{a^2+c^2}, f=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}</math> of the base triangle exist, e.g. <math>a=240,b=117,c=44,d=125,e=244,f=267</math> (discovered 1719 by Halcke). Here are a few more examples with integer legs and sides.
     a        b        c        d        e        f 
----
    240      117       44      125      244      267
    275      252      240      348      365      373
    480      234       88      250      488      534
    550      504      480      696      730      746
    693      480      140      500      707      843
    720      351      132      375      732      801
    720      132       85      157      725      732
    792      231      160      281      808      825
    825      756      720     1044     1095     1119
    960      468      176      500      976     1068
   1100     1008      960     1392     1460     1492
   1155     1100     1008     1492     1533     1595
   1200      585      220      625     1220     1335
   1375     1260     1200     1740     1825     1865
   1386      960      280     1000     1414     1686
   1440      702      264      750     1464     1602
   1440      264      170      314     1450     1464
Notice that some of these are multiples of smaller ones. Note also {{OEIS link|A031173}}.

===Integer faces===
Trirectangular tetrahedra with integer faces <math>T_c, T_a, T_b, T_0</math> and altitude ''h'' exist, e.g. <math>a=42,b=28,c=14,T_c=588,T_a=196,T_b=294,T_0=686,h=12</math> without or <math>a=156,b=80,c=65,T_c=6240,T_a=2600,T_b=5070,T_0=8450,h=48</math> with coprime <math>a,b,c</math>.
